newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Howard says climate still good for low rates.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Howard says climate still good for low rates.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Friday that the climate was good for maintaining low interest rates.
"The climate is still very good for the maintenance of low interest rates," Howard told reporters, when asked whether today's balance of payments figures had any implications for interest rates.
He said the figures, which showed a widening in the current account deficit in October to A$1.788 billion, did not have any interest rate implications.
"I don't think today's figures on their own have any significance at all (for rates)," Howard said.

Asked about Reserve Bank of Australia's (RBA) governor Ian Macfarlane's statement that unemployment was in greater need of improvement than inflation, Howard said he welcomed the importance the central bank was placing on employment growth.
"I certainly agree that the most important social objective in Australia is reducing unemployment," Howard said.

"But of course, as he knows better than anybody, and has said in the past on many ocassion, keeping inflation down is a pre-requisite to a strong growing economy, which in turn generates jobs," he said.
Macfarlane said in a speech on Thursday night that the unemployment rate at 8.8 percent was too high and is in greater need of improvement than inflation, which was at 2.4 percent.
